fatal_errors: The hypothesis centers on hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10, whereas the demonstrated design space and experiment concern as-cast Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloys, specifically Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 versus equimolar NbMoTaVW.

It proposes Ta/V enrichment and Mo/W depletion for HfNbTiVAl10 even though Ta, Mo, and W are not constituents of the stated starting alloy; this would constitute an undefined change to a different alloy system.
The target method screened compositions using rule-of-mixtures Young's modulus, VEC, and density; it did not establish that VEC predicts real yield strength or fracture toughness.
The proposed tensile and fracture-toughness setting does not reconstruct the reported room-temperature, quasi-static compression tests.
The claimed ±10% accuracy and threefold efficiency gain are invented and have no cited or supplied evidence.
No supporting prior evidence is identified, and the target study explicitly notes that microstructure, processing history, defects, and phase effects were absent from its simple design model.
explanation: The response retains only the broad idea of rapid VEC-guided composition screening and correctly recognizes that disruption of microstructure could invalidate empirical correlations. It misses the central reconstruction: validation of an averaged iso-strain/iso-stress rule-of-mixtures modulus model on roughly 130–132 HEAs, screening 38,326 Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions, and selecting Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 for low VEC with relatively high modulus. It also substitutes tensile strength and fracture toughness for the demonstrated compressive yield strength and fracture strain. The actual evidence was a single-phase BCC as-cast alloy tested at room temperature and 5 × 10^-4 s^-1, yielding 1115 ± 18 MPa and reaching 35.7 ± 0.9% compressive fracture strain, compared with approximately 1246 MPa and 2% for equimolar NbMoTaVW. The blinded benchmark has measurable endpoints and a numerical falsification threshold, giving it some discriminability, but it lacks sample counts, split procedures, matched processing controls, and a valid basis for expecting VEC alone to predict toughness. Its central performance thresholds are unsupported rather than evidence-based.
